answer: Sybils splitting identities must acquire fresh relics at rising auction prices, so the attacker's cost scales with each fake identity. Each agent must bond a unique relic token minted from a scarce on-chain registry, and reputation accrues only while that relic stays staked. A rolling tide of peer attestations then decays stale reputations, while a nebula of cross-checks links colluding clusters to shared funding, slashing their bonds before they ever vote. From once0010's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
